lines.trans: Two rings on a quiet Sunday: that double bell is definitely Room Four.

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Right on time! Look who is coming down the stairs with a green book!
I pressed the bell only once upstairs, Mateo, and your friendly wire rang twice as usual.

words.gloss: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)

lines.trans: If Room Four rang only once, madam, I would think it was broken.
Here is the cloth-bound herb book from the bookshop on Calle de los Tilos!
Look at the gold letters on the green cover: Courtyard Herbs and Blossoms.
Check inside the front cover first: old neighbours always wrote down their number there.

words.gloss: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)

lines.trans: Good eye, Mateo! Written in pencil in the corner is our exact number from thirty years ago!

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
ago (hace treinta años = thirty years ago)

Turn the pages slowly over the desk so no dry leaf falls onto the floor.
Wait, the book falls open all by itself near chapter seven on summer mint!
Let us carry it straight to Rocio in Room Nine before anyone blows hard!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.

examples.text: Ayer abrimos la tienda temprano.
examples.trans: Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.

examples.text: ¿Hay alguien en recepción?
examples.trans: Is anyone at the front desk?

meanings.note: Points to a place farther away from both speakers.

examples.text: La farmacia está allí en la esquina.
examples.trans: The pharmacy is over there on the corner.

examples.text: Vivimos allí durante seis años.
examples.trans: We lived there for six years.

meanings.note: Muy amable is a warm thank-you ('very kind of you').

examples.text: Es una pieza amable.
examples.trans: It is a kind piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Placed after a noun, means 'historic' or 'old-fashioned'.

examples.text: Es una pieza antigua.
examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: Encantada, Tomás, ¡siempre que nadie hable de vender pianos antiguos!
examples.trans: Gladly, Tomas, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

meanings.note: Everyday word in Spain for writing down a note or phone number.

examples.text: Apunto la dirección en un papel.
examples.trans: I jot down the address on a piece of paper.

examples.text: ¿Apuntaste el nombre del cliente?
examples.trans: Did you write down the guest's name?

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.text: Las habitaciones están arriba.
examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.

examples.text: Mira arriba hacia el balcón.
examples.trans: Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.text: El año está aquí.
examples.trans: The year is here.

examples.text: Vemos los años desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

meanings.note: Bajo llave means 'under lock and key'; as an adjective (bajo/baja), means 'low' or 'ground' (planta baja).

examples.text: Nos sentamos bajo el limonero.
examples.trans: We sit under the lemon tree.

examples.text: Guarda la caja bajo llave.
examples.trans: Keep the box under lock and key.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.text: ¡Buenos días a todos!
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!

examples.text: Hace muy buen tiempo hoy.
examples.trans: The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Electrical cord or wire.

examples.text: El cable está aquí.
examples.trans: The cord is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cables desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cords from the door.

meanings.note: With se + indirect object (se le cayó), expresses accidental dropping.

examples.text: La lluvia cae sobre el tejado.
examples.trans: The rain falls on the tiled roof.

examples.text: Se me cayeron las monedas.
examples.trans: I accidentally dropped the coins.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.text: La calle está aquí.
examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.en: episode of a television or streaming series
meanings.note: In Peninsular Spanish, capítulo is the everyday word for a TV show episode (more common in casual speech than episodio).

meanings.en: chapter of a book or life stage
meanings.note: Standard literary and figurative sense ('cerrar un capítulo' = 'to close a chapter').

examples.text: Ponme otro capítulo.
examples.trans: Put on another episode for me.

examples.text: Nos vimos toda la temporada capítulo tras capítulo en una sola tarde.
examples.trans: We binge-watched the whole season episode after episode in a single afternoon.

meanings.note: Cerca de + noun = near something; de cerca = up close.

examples.text: Mi familia vive muy cerca.
examples.trans: My family lives very nearby.

examples.text: Mira esta página de cerca.
examples.trans: Look closely at this page.

meanings.note: Unaccented como compares or gives a reason (distinct from interrogative cómo).

examples.text: Está fría como el agua del río.
examples.trans: It is as cold as river water.

examples.text: Todo funciona como debe ser.
examples.trans: Everything works just as it should.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Tenemos cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Dentro de + time means 'in (after) a certain amount of time'.

examples.text: Hay cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: There are four tables inside.

examples.text: Vuelvo dentro de diez minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday single-word opposite of rápido.

examples.text: Camina despacio por las escaleras.
examples.trans: Walk slowly on the stairs.

examples.text: Gira la rueda muy despacio.
examples.trans: Turn the wheel very slowly.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (salir directo = walk straight out).

examples.text: Es una pieza directa.
examples.trans: It is a direct piece.

examples.text: Sí, Rocío. Aunque dé media vuelta y salga directo por la puerta.
examples.trans: Yes, Rocio. Even if he turns around and walks straight back out the gate.

meanings.note: El doble de... means 'double the amount of...'.

examples.text: El doble está aquí.
examples.trans: The double is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dobles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doubles from the door.

meanings.note: El domingo = on Sunday; los domingos = on Sundays.

examples.text: El domingo está aquí.
examples.trans: The Sunday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los domingos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Sundays from the door.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Very frequent in the fixed phrase sin duda ('without a doubt; definitely').

examples.text: Esa es sin duda la vieja librería de segunda mano.
examples.trans: That is definitely the old second-hand bookshop.

examples.text: Si tienes alguna duda sobre la ruta, mira el mapa.
examples.trans: If you have any doubt about the route, check the map.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Built from cuaderno ('notebook / quire'); encuadernado en tela means 'cloth-bound'.

examples.text: Compré un libro de hierbas encuadernado en tela verde en la librería.
examples.trans: I bought a herb book bound in green cloth at the bookshop.

examples.text: En aquel taller antiguo todavía encuadernan los libros a mano.
examples.trans: In that old workshop they still bind books by hand.

meanings.note: Often singular (la escalera) or plural (las escaleras) for a staircase.

examples.text: La escalera está aquí.
examples.trans: The stairs is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escaleras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stairss from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle escrito.

examples.text: Escribo la nota con lápiz azul.
examples.trans: I write the note in blue pencil.

examples.text: Mi hermano me escribió una postal corta.
examples.trans: My brother wrote me a short postcard.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.text: La esquina está aquí.
examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Wooden wall or cupboard shelf.

examples.text: El estante está aquí.
examples.trans: The shelf is here.

examples.text: Vemos los estantes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shelves from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Used alone as an enthusiastic 'Exactly!'.

examples.text: Es una pieza exacta.
examples.trans: It is an exact piece.

examples.text: ¡Exacto! Ya eres una más del equipo.
examples.trans: Exactly! You are already one of the team.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la flor, las flores.

examples.text: La flor está aquí.
examples.trans: The flower is here.

examples.text: Vemos las flores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the flowers from the door.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (llover/discutir fuerte).

examples.text: Es una pieza fuerte.
examples.trans: It is a strong piece.

examples.text: ¡Rápido, ciérralo! Vamos a subirlo... esperad, ¿qué es ese golpe metálico tan fuerte?
examples.trans: Quick, close it! Let us take it upstairs... wait, what is that loud metallic bang?

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.text: La habitación está aquí.
examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: Llegó hace diez minutos.
examples.trans: She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Garden herbs or meadow grass.

examples.text: La hierba está aquí.
examples.trans: The herb is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hierbas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the herbs from the door.

meanings.note: Means both a tree leaf and a single sheet of paper.

examples.text: La hoja está aquí.
examples.trans: The leaf is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hojas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the leaves from the door.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.text: La llave está justo aquí.
examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Tu letra means 'your handwriting'.

examples.text: La letra está aquí.
examples.trans: The handwriting is here.

examples.text: Vemos las letras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the handwritings from the door.

meanings.note: In Spain both a bookshop and a piece of furniture full of shelves for books. Not a library (biblioteca).

examples.text: Compro el libro en la librería de la esquina.
examples.trans: I buy the book at the bookshop on the corner.

examples.text: Tenemos una librería grande en el salón.
examples.trans: We have a big bookcase in the living room.

meanings.note: Libro de reservas = reservation ledger.

examples.text: El libro está aquí.
examples.trans: The book is here.

examples.text: Vemos los libros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the books from the door.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: llegué.

examples.text: Siempre llego diez minutos temprano.
examples.trans: I always arrive ten minutes early.

examples.text: El tren de Madrid llegó en punto.
examples.trans: The train from Madrid arrived on the dot.

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.

examples.text: ¡Hasta luego, que tengas buen día!
examples.trans: See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: Plural los lápices; a lápiz = in pencil.

examples.text: El lápiz está aquí.
examples.trans: The pencil is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lápices desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pencils from the door.

meanings.note: Té de menta = mint tea.

examples.text: La menta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The mint is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la menta.
examples.trans: We talk about the mint.

meanings.note: Dining, cafe, or courtyard table.

examples.text: La mesa está aquí.
examples.trans: The table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tables from the door.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

ninguno.gloss: no; none; neither (ninguno de los dos)

meanings.en: no; none; neither (ninguno de los dos)
meanings.note: Shortens to ningún before masculine singular nouns (ningún edificio).

examples.text: Ningún edificio antiguo se derriba aquí.
examples.trans: No historic building is torn down here.

examples.text: Ninguno de los dos se marchó.
examples.trans: Neither of the two walked away.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.text: Nuestra posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.

examples.text: Nuestros vecinos toman café aquí.
examples.trans: Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Las nueve = nine o'clock.

examples.text: El tren llega a las nueve en punto.
examples.trans: The train arrives at nine on the dot.

examples.text: Vimos un nueve sobre diez.
examples.trans: We saw a nine out of ten.

meanings.note: Written after street names in Spanish addresses (Calle Mayor número ocho).

examples.text: El número está aquí.
examples.trans: The number is here.

examples.text: Vemos los números desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the numbers from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los ojos.

examples.text: El ojo está aquí.
examples.trans: The eye is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ojos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the eyes from the door.

meanings.en: gold (precious metal, color, or something of great value)
meanings.note: Masculine noun. Frequently used figuratively in the idiom 'valer oro' ('to be worth its weight in gold / to be priceless'), as when Paquita savors the fresh country air of her hometown.

meanings.en: oros (suit of golden coins in the Spanish card deck)
meanings.note: In the plural ('los oros'), refers to the suit of coins in the traditional Spanish deck of cards ('la baraja española').

examples.text: Este aire... (ASPIRA) Este aire vale oro.
examples.trans: This air... (INHALES) This air is worth its weight in gold.

examples.text: Esa representante tiene un corazón de oro aunque a veces pierda los nervios.
examples.trans: That talent agent has a heart of gold even though she loses her temper sometimes.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.text: ¡Pase, por favor, y siéntese!
examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: El patio está aquí.
examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

pensar.gloss: to think; to plan to (pensar + infinitive)

meanings.en: to think; to plan to (pensar + infinitive)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: pienso).

examples.text: Pienso abrir la cafetería a las ocho.
examples.trans: I plan to open the cafe at eight.

examples.text: ¿Qué piensas de esta pintura azul?
examples.trans: What do you think of this blue paint?

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.

examples.text: La primera habitación está libre.
examples.trans: The first room is vacant.

pulsar.gloss: to press; to push (a button or switch)

meanings.en: to press; to push (a button or switch)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Pulsa el timbre de latón si la puerta está cerrada.
examples.trans: Press the brass bell if the door is closed.

examples.text: Clara pulsó el interruptor y se encendió la luz.
examples.trans: Clara pressed the switch and the light came on.

meanings.note: La segunda página = page two.

examples.text: La página está aquí.
examples.trans: The page is here.

examples.text: Vemos las páginas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pages from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Plural quiénes; ¿de quién es? = whose is it?

examples.text: ¿Quién ha dejado este sobre aquí?
examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?

examples.text: ¿De quién es esta maleta azul?
examples.trans: Whose blue suitcase is this?

meanings.note: Irregular past participle of romper.

examples.text: Es una pieza rota.
examples.trans: It is a broken piece.

examples.text: Esta casa sobrevivió a ochenta inviernos y ayer a una válvula rota de la caldera.
examples.trans: This house survived eighty winters and one broken boiler valve yesterday.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

secar.gloss: to dry; to wipe dry (secarse = to dry out)

meanings.en: to dry; to wipe dry (secarse = to dry out)
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (sequé, seque).

examples.text: Seca bien las bisagras antes de dar la pintura.
examples.trans: Dry the hinges thoroughly before applying paint.

examples.text: Con este sol la ropa tendida se seca enseguida.
examples.trans: In this sunshine the hanging laundry dries right away.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.text: La señora está aquí.
examples.trans: The madam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the madams from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.text: Avísame si necesitas otra manta.
examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

siempre.gloss: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)

meanings.en: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)
meanings.note: Opposite of nunca.

examples.text: El patio siempre está tranquilo.
examples.trans: The courtyard is always quiet.

examples.text: Ven siempre que quieras tomar café.
examples.trans: Come whenever you want to have coffee.

meanings.note: Las siete y cuarto = seven fifteen.

examples.text: La habitación siete mira al patio.
examples.trans: Room seven overlooks the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las siete y media.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at seven thirty.

meanings.note: Followed by bare nouns (sin azúcar, sin sal) or infinitives (sin abrir = unopened).

examples.text: Tomo el té sin azúcar, gracias.
examples.trans: I take my tea without sugar, thank you.

examples.text: Salió de casa sin abrigo.
examples.trans: He left home without a coat.

sobre.gloss: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)

meanings.en: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)
meanings.note: Sobre todo = above all / mostly; also a homograph noun el sobre ('envelope').

examples.text: Deja la llave sobre el mostrador.
examples.trans: Leave the key on the counter.

examples.text: Sacó nueve sobre diez en la prueba.
examples.trans: She scored nine out of ten on the test.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.text: Solo necesito cinco minutos más.
examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.

examples.text: Queda una sola habitación libre.
examples.trans: Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Used for the wind blowing (sopla el viento) and for blowing on hot soup or birthday candles.

examples.text: Si mañana por la tarde sopla el viento, las cuerdas no se moverán.
examples.trans: If the wind blows tomorrow afternoon, the cords will not budge.

examples.text: Sopla un poco la cuchara antes de tomar la sopa caliente.
examples.trans: Blow on the spoon a little before taking the hot soup.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave, señora.
examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Las tablas del suelo = the floorboards.

examples.text: El gato duerme en el suelo.
examples.trans: The cat sleeps on the floor.

examples.text: Limpio el suelo de la cocina.
examples.trans: I'm cleaning the kitchen floor.

meanings.note: The lid of a box, pot or piano; in a Spanish bar also a small plate of food.

examples.text: ¿Dónde está la tapa de la olla?
examples.trans: Where is the lid of the pot?

examples.text: Pedimos una tapa de tortilla.
examples.trans: We order a small plate of tortilla.

meanings.note: Material for clothes, curtains or old cable covers.

examples.text: Esta camisa es de una tela muy suave.
examples.trans: This shirt is made of a very soft fabric.

examples.text: Compro tela para las cortinas.
examples.trans: I'm buying fabric for the curtains.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: ¿Qué tiempo hace? asks about the weather; a tiempo = on time.

examples.text: El tiempo está aquí.
examples.trans: The time is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tiempos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the times from the door.

meanings.note: Tocar el timbre = ring the bell.

examples.text: El timbre está aquí.
examples.trans: The bell is here.

examples.text: Vemos los timbres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bells from the door.

tocar.gloss: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)

meanings.en: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: toqué.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: Someone just rang the bell.

examples.text: De niño tocaba el piano los viernes.
examples.trans: As a boy he played the piano on Fridays.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.text: Es una pieza tranquila.
examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: Treinta y cinco = thirty-five.

examples.text: Nos dan treinta días de plazo.
examples.trans: They give us thirty days' notice.

examples.text: Son las nueve y treinta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is nine thirty-five.

meanings.note: Unaccented possessive (tu llave / tus llaves), distinct from accented pronoun tú.

examples.text: ¿Dónde está tu caja de herramientas?
examples.trans: Where is your toolbox?

examples.text: Reconocí tu letra enseguida.
examples.trans: I recognized your handwriting right away.

meanings.note: Feminine counterpart of el tío ('uncle').

examples.text: La tía de Ernesto tocaba el piano todos los viernes.
examples.trans: Ernesto's aunt played the piano every Friday.

examples.text: Mi tía prepara el mejor bizcocho de limón del barrio.
examples.trans: My aunt bakes the best lemon sponge cake in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Feminine: la vecina.

examples.text: El vecino está aquí.
examples.trans: The neighbour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los vecinos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neighbours from the door.

meanings.note: El verano que viene = next summer.

examples.text: El verano está aquí.
examples.trans: The summer is here.

examples.text: Vemos los veranos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the summers from the door.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.text: La verdad está aquí.
examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza verde.
examples.trans: It is a green piece.

examples.text: Mateo, ¿me oyes? ¡Acabo de pasar la farmacia verde!
examples.trans: Mateo, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.text: La vez está aquí.
examples.trans: The time / occasion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las veces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the time / occasions from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.
